declarations.docstring: The natural-number measure assigned to an object by its composition factors.
The composition-factor measure is additive across a short exact sequence.
The composition-factor measure of a binary biproduct is the sum of the two measures.
An object has vanishing composition-factor measure exactly when it is zero.
With a finite-dimensional subobject order, zero measure characterizes zero objects.
A zero object has zero composition-factor measure.
The composition-factor measure is monotone under inclusion of subobjects.
Extending a subobject adds the measure of the associated cokernel.
Every nonzero object has positive composition-factor measure.
A simple object contributes one unit to the composition-factor measure.
A strict inclusion of subobjects strictly increases the composition-factor measure.
A decreasing sequence of subobjects eventually stops changing.
An increasing sequence of subobjects eventually stops changing.
The image subobjects of successive powers of an endomorphism eventually stabilize.
Some positive power has both image and kernel subobjects unchanged after doubling its exponent.
The kernel subobjects of successive powers of an endomorphism eventually stabilize.
At a positive iterate, the canonical composite through its image is invertible.
The subobject order of a zero object is finite-dimensional.
For a finite-dimensional subobject order, its top height is finite.
Images of increasing powers of an endomorphism form a decreasing subobject sequence.
Kernels of increasing powers of an endomorphism form an increasing subobject sequence.
Strict descent among subobjects is well-founded.
